items.title: CONTRIBUTING.md says tqdm and mcp are the only runtime dependencies, but pyproject also requires httpx
items.body:
## Problem

The Style section of `CONTRIBUTING.md` (lines 75 to 77) says:

> Keep runtime dependencies minimal. `tqdm` (progress bar) and `mcp` (the MCP server SDK) are the only two; anything new must justify its weight.

But `pyproject.toml` (the `[project]` `dependencies` list, lines 22 to 26) declares three runtime dependencies:

```toml
dependencies = [
    "httpx>=0.28",
    "tqdm>=4.66",
    "mcp>=2.0,<3",
]
```

`httpx` is a real runtime dependency, not an optional extra: `taken/transport.py` and the GraphQL httpx path (`TAKEN_TRANSPORT=httpx`, `TAKEN_GRAPHQL_TRANSPORT=httpx`) import it during normal operation, and `tests/test_graphql_httpx.py` covers that path. The CONTRIBUTING text predates the httpx addition and was never updated, so a new contributor reading it gets a wrong picture of what the package depends on, and of what "justify its weight" has already been granted to.

`docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` is a byte-identical copy of `CONTRIBUTING.md` and carries the same stale sentence.

## Expected behavior

The Style section names all three current runtime dependencies (`httpx`, `tqdm`, `mcp`), each with a short note on what it is used for, matching the `dependencies` list in `pyproject.toml`. Both copies of the file say the same thing.

## Acceptance criteria

- The Style section of `CONTRIBUTING.md` no longer claims there are only two runtime dependencies, and its list matches `pyproject.toml`.
- `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` is updated with the identical change, so the two files remain byte-identical.
- No other claim in the section changes: the "anything new must justify its weight" rule and the dev-tools sentence stay as they are.

## Likely files

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` (Style section)
- `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` (identical copy)

## Testing

Docs-only change; no test suite run is needed. Verify with `diff CONTRIBUTING.md docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` (no output) and by comparing the dependency names in the updated text against the `dependencies` list in `pyproject.toml`.

_Found during an automated audit of the codebase._

items.title: MCP server is never built or tested in CI
items.body:
## Problem
`ci.yml` has jobs for the frontend, the TypeScript client, the Python client and the pipeline. It has none for `mcp-server`, so its vitest suite never runs and nothing checks that it compiles. The package also has a few loose ends that a CI job would surface.

## Evidence
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` jobs: `frontend` (`:11`), `client-typescript` (`:34`), `client-python` (`:68`), `pipeline` (`:89`). `git grep -i mcp -- .github` has no hits.
- `mcp-server/package.json` has `build` (`tsc`) and `test` (`vitest run`) scripts.
- `mcp-server/README.md:16` installs with `npx -y ucip-mcp`. `https://registry.npmjs.org/ucip-mcp` returns 404 (checked 2026-10-23), and `README.md:133` says the server is not yet published.
- Smaller gaps: `package.json:25` declares `zod`, which nothing in `src` imports (the SDK depends on it itself); `src/client.ts:60` calls `fetch` with no timeout; `src/index.ts:181` hardcodes version `0.1.0`.
- The lockfile pins `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.30.1, which `npm audit` flags as high (advisories about the OAuth client and experimental tasks; the imports at `index.ts:20-27` use neither; exposure not assessed).

## Why it matters
The server is the part of the project an assistant talks to directly, and its tests are the only check on the caveat text it attaches to answers.

## Proposed fix
Add an `mcp-server` job modelled on `client-typescript` (`ci.yml:34-62`): Node 24, `npm ci`, `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `npm test`. In the same PR or follow-ups: `npm audit fix` for the SDK, an `AbortSignal.timeout` in `client.ts`, read the version from `package.json`, drop the direct `zod` dependency, and change the README install to run-from-source until it is published.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CI shows an `mcp-server` job that runs `npm ci`, a type-check and `npm test`, and passes.
- [ ] Breaking an assertion in `index.test.ts` makes that job fail.
- [ ] `client.ts` aborts a request after a timeout, covered by a test with a stubbed `fetch`.
- [ ] `cd mcp-server && npm audit --omit=dev` reports no high findings.

## Notes
Size S. Related: #102 (closed, built the server), #103 (open, the TypeScript client is also unpublished). Where to start: copy the `client-typescript` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; prove it with `cd mcp-server && npm ci && npm test` locally and the PR's CI run.

items.title: MCP server and client READMEs still say the index has seven indicators
items.body:
## Problem
The index has scored five indicators since 2026-10-17 (`docs/DATA-DICTIONARY.md:25`, `pipeline/_indicators.py`). Four shipped texts still say seven. The MCP server attaches the wrong count to four of its five tools.

## Evidence
```
mcp-server/src/index.ts:37        "It combines seven standardised indicators with PCA-derived weights"
clients/python/README.md:65       "rather than a real combination of seven"
clients/typescript/README.md:63   "rather than a real combination of seven"
DESIGN.md:73                      "then the seven contribution bars (F2)"
```
`INDEX_CAVEAT` (`mcp-server/src/index.ts:35-38`) is added to `list_wards`, `get_ward`, `lookup_ward` and `get_methodology`. `GET /api/v1/meta` already says "five standardised indicators". The `ucip` 0.1.0 package on PyPI carries the Python README.

## Why it matters
Every MCP answer repeats a count that contradicts the dataset, and a model will quote it.

## Proposed fix
Change "seven" to "five" in the four places. Add a one-line test that `INDEX_CAVEAT` contains "five" and not "seven". Leave the PyPI version bump to a maintainer.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `git grep -n -i seven -- mcp-server clients DESIGN.md` shows no mention of the indicator count (the unrelated "seven of them" at `clients/typescript/src/index.ts:6` stays).
- [ ] `cd mcp-server && npm test` passes with the new assertion.

## Notes
Size S. Related: #103 (open, publishing the TypeScript client; fix the README before it ships). Where to start: `mcp-server/src/index.ts:35-38`, then prove it with `git grep -n -i seven -- mcp-server clients DESIGN.md` and `cd mcp-server && npm test`.

items.title: `config --mcp-providers "core,"` saves a builtin MCP server with an empty name
items.body:
`octomind config --mcp-providers "core,"` (note the trailing comma) saves a builtin MCP server whose name is the empty string. `--mcp-providers ""` does the same, and also removes every other configured server. The command reports success either way. At runtime the blank server matches no builtin and quietly provides no tools. A blank name should be rejected with nothing saved, the way `--mcp-server` already rejects one.

Where
- `src/commands/config.rs:239` in `execute`: `let server_names: Vec<String> = providers.split(',').map(|s| s.trim().to_string()).collect();`. Empty segments are kept.
- `:240` then runs `config.mcp.servers.clear();` before anything is checked. `:243` creates `let server = McpServerConfig::builtin(server_name, DEFAULT_MCP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, Vec::new());` for each name, `""` included.
- At runtime an unknown builtin name only produces a debug log: `src/mcp/mod.rs:426-427`, `other => {` / `crate::log_debug!("Unknown builtin server: {}", other);`.
- The neighbouring flag already handles this: `src/commands/config.rs:259-264`, `if name.is_empty() {` … `block_close_err("config", "mcp server name cannot be empty");` … `return Ok(());`. It is covered by `test_mcp_server_blank_name_is_rejected`.
- Permalink: https://github.com/Muvon/octomind/blob/6ce0ded12211d64add86336d627fbfea7fedc210/src/commands/config.rs#L238-L264

Fix
- In the `--mcp-providers` branch of `execute`, check the names before `config.mcp.servers.clear()`. If any name is empty after trimming, report it with `block_open` / `block_close_err` and `return Ok(())` without saving, like the `--mcp-server` branch does.

Tests in `src/commands/config_tests.rs`, next to `test_mcp_providers_replace_servers_with_dedup`, mirroring `test_mcp_server_blank_name_is_rejected`:
- `mcp_providers = Some("core,")`, `Some("")` and `Some(" , core")` each leave no saved config (`!saved_config_path(&dir).exists()`).
- `Some("core,runtime")` still saves both servers.

Out of scope
- Rejecting names that aren't real builtins (only `core`, `runtime`, `orchestration` and `agent` exist today). That needs a decision on where the list lives, so leave it for a separate change.

New to the project? Start with CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md. Two conventions trip people up: tests go in sibling `*_tests.rs` files, and code is indented with tabs. Before opening a PR, run `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`. No API key is needed. Comment here to claim the issue before opening a PR. This issue is meant for a person learning the codebase, so disclose any AI help, and don't let an agent claim or solve it. Put `Closes #<this issue>` in your PR description.

items.title: MCP initialize returns no server instructions; point the client at kb_orient

milestone.description: Follow-ups after 0.26.0: open 0.25.9 and 0.26 items that did not land by 2026-10-22.

items.body:
Split from #1286 (polish from the 2026-10-23 hallway test). A small, self-contained first issue.

**What happens.** An MCP client that connects to `pyrite mcp` gets no server `instructions` in the `initialize` result. The one hint about where to start ("Use this first") is inside the `kb_orient` tool description, one of 66 to 106 tools. Clients that show server instructions to the model (most do) show nothing. Reproduced on `dev` at d66c4555 with the Python `mcp` client:

```python
init = await session.initialize()
init.instructions        # -> None
```

**What to change.** `PyriteMCPServer.build_sdk_server` in `pyrite/server/mcp_server.py` builds the SDK server with `Server(f"pyrite-{self.tier}")` (about line 2829). The installed SDK's `Server.__init__` takes `instructions=`. Pass a short text. It should say:
- call `kb_orient` first: with no arguments it lists the KBs you can read and the operational contracts; with `kb_name` it describes one KB;
- the tier this server runs at (`self.tier`), and that tools of a higher tier are not listed;
- errors come back as a result with `error`, `error_code`, `retryable` (see `kb_orient`).

Keep it under about 600 characters. Keep the text in one constant, and do not repeat the tool descriptions.

**Acceptance.**
- A test starts the server over stdio, or builds it through `build_sdk_server`, and asserts that the `initialize` result has `instructions` naming `kb_orient` and the tier. It fails today. `tests/test_mcp_read_scoping.py` already does a real `initialize` round trip; model the test on it.
- The text is the same for every tier apart from the tier name. It is built once per connection, like the rest of the server.

**Files.** `pyrite/server/mcp_server.py` and one test. About 15 lines plus the test.

**Out of scope.** The tool descriptions themselves. `kb_link` needing `source_kb` is already in its `required` list. A tool above the connected tier answering `UNKNOWN_TOOL` is #1276.


---
_Filed by the maintainer's architect agent (automated), 2026-10-23._

---

## Groom 2026-10-23

*Automated groom (architect agent). Checked on `dev` at 3f73c653. No open PR covers this issue now: PR #1296 carried an earlier version of it and has since been cut down to #1290.*

small: 2 and 3 only

### 2. What the code does today
- `PyriteMCPServer.build_sdk_server` (`pyrite/server/mcp_server.py`, the `Server(f"pyrite-{self.tier}")` call at line 2829) passes no `instructions`. The installed SDK's `Server.__init__` takes `instructions: str | None` (checked with `inspect.signature`).
- **One place for both transports.** Stdio (`main`, about line 2942) and HTTP MCP (`pyrite/server/mcp_routes.py`, about line 379, one `PyriteMCPServer` per tier) both build through `build_sdk_server`. The text set there reaches every client.

### 3. Invariant and surfaces
**Invariant:** every MCP connection's `initialize` result tells the client where to start (`kb_orient`), which tier it is connected at, and the error shape. The text comes from one constant.

**Shapes:** tiers `read`, `write` and `admin`; transports stdio and HTTP; a client that ignores `instructions` (no change for it).

**Surfaces:** MCP only. The tool list and the descriptions stay unchanged. The characterization goldens for `initialize`, if any capture it, change on purpose; say so in the PR.

```
Acceptance:   as above, parametrised over the three tiers on stdio, and one HTTP round trip; fails today (instructions is None)
Regimes:      text length (keep it under about 600 characters; assert it)
Touches:      existing: pyrite/server/mcp_server.py   new: tests/test_mcp_initialize_instructions.py
Sequence:     independent
Model:        sonnet
heavy:        no
Cold read:    no
Out of scope: tool descriptions; a tool above the tier answering UNKNOWN_TOOL (#1276); kb_timeline's kb_name (#1233)
Decision:     none
```

**good first issue: kept.**

items.title: kb_registry_health and kb_stats report entry_count 0 and healthy:false after MCP writes

milestone.description: Follow-ups after 0.26.0: open 0.25.9 and 0.26 items that did not land by 2026-10-22.

items.body:
**What happens.** After entries are created over MCP, the registry counters stay at their init values and `kb_registry_health` says the KB is unhealthy, while the index is fine.

```
# admin tier, new connection each time, after 3 kb_create calls in an earlier session
kb_registry_health {"name":"scratch-a"}
-> "healthy":false,"file_count":2,"entry_count":0,"last_indexed":"<the init time>"
kb_stats  -> entry_count:0, actual_count:2
pyrite index health -k scratch-a -> unindexed_files: 0
```

Entries are searchable and `kb_orient` reports `total_entries` correctly, so only the registry counter is stale. Seen on three separate connections. An agent that trusts `healthy:false` reindexes for nothing.

**Expected.** `entry_count` equals the real count (or the field is computed, not stored), and `healthy` is true when `index health` is clean.

**Minimal repro.** `pyrite init -t research -p kb-a -n scratch-a`; `pyrite mcp --tier admin`; `kb_create` two entries; call `kb_registry_health` and `kb_stats`.

**Shapes this must hold for.** MCP `kb_registry_health`, `kb_stats` (`entry_count` vs `actual_count`); the same counters read by CLI `pyrite kb list` / `kb health` and REST KB listing; writes by MCP `kb_create`/`kb_update`/`kb_delete`, CLI `create`/`delete`, and a hand edit followed by `index sync`. Test: after each write path, the counters equal `actual_count`.

Source: `feedback/2026-10-23-hallway-mcp-memory-agent.md`, Friction 1.



## Groom 2026-10-23

*Automated groom (architect agent). Reproduced on `dev` at `d66c4555` with a scratch `HOME`; anchors checked against `376d21d2`.*

**Principle at stake: 4** (derive, do not write: a count is computed from the index, never stored and left to drift), and **8** (`index health` already gives a verdict; `kb_registry_health` keeps a second rule).

**The user's model.** "`kb_registry_health` tells me whether this KB's index is fine."
**The implementation model.** The count is computed from the `entry` table when it is read. `healthy` is the verdict `index health` gives (`health_verdict`, `pyrite/services/index_health.py`).

### 2. What the code does today

- Reproduced: `init -t research`, then two `kb_create` over MCP. `kb_registry_health {"name":"scratch-a"}` returns `"healthy":false,"file_count":2,"entry_count":0`. `kb_stats` returns `entry_count: 0, actual_count: 2`. CLI `pyrite kb health -k scratch-a` gives the same `healthy: false`, while `pyrite index health -k scratch-a` reports `"status": "healthy"`.
- **The stored count is written only by a sync.** `KB.entry_count` (`pyrite/storage/models.py:34`) is set by `update_kb_indexed` (`pyrite/storage/kb_ops.py:311`), which only `IndexManager.sync_kb` calls (`pyrite/storage/index.py:1096`). Writes through `KBService` upsert rows and never touch it. This is correct per principle 4: the fix is to stop reading the column, not to write it more often.
- **Half of this is already fixed.** `KBRegistryService.list_kbs` (`pyrite/services/kb_registry_service.py:98`, the query at :134) derives `live_entry_count` with a subquery (#632). So `kb list` and `kb_orient` are right, and they are the pattern to copy.
- `KBRegistryService.get_kb` (`:180`, `"entries": kb.entry_count`) and `KBRegistryService.health_kb` (`:527`, `entry_count = kb.entry_count`) still read the column. `healthy` (`:545`) is "files within 10% of the stored count", and the file count is every `*.md` outside dot-folders. A KB with a README or `_index.md` files is "unhealthy" by this rule even when the index is complete.
- `get_kb_stats` (`kb_ops.py:250`) returns `SELECT k.*`, so every stats reader carries both the stale `entry_count` and the correct `actual_count`.

### 3. Invariant and surfaces

**Invariant.** Every KB count a surface shows is the index's count when it is read, and every health verdict is the one `health_verdict` gives.

**Enumeration source:** the readers of `KB.entry_count` (grep `entry_count` under `pyrite/`):

| Reader | Surfaces | State |
|---|---|---|
| `KBRegistryService.health_kb` | MCP `kb_registry_health` (`mcp_server.py:2110`), CLI `kb health` (`kb_commands.py:518`), REST `GET /api/kbs/{name}/health` (`endpoints/kbs.py:96`, `kb_health`) | stale |
| `KBRegistryService.get_kb` | REST `GET /api/kbs/{name}` (`endpoints/kbs.py:76`, `get_kb`); CLI `kb remove` (existence only, safe) | stale |
| `get_kb_stats` | MCP `kb_stats`, REST `/api/stats` (`endpoints/admin.py:64`), CLI `index stats` (prints `actual_count`, safe) | stale `entry_count` field |
| `KBService.list_kbs` fallback (`kb_service.py:770`, no registry) | the same callers when no registry is set | stale |
| `KBRegistryService.list_kbs` | `kb list`, `kb_orient`, `kb_list` | correct |

**Shapes** for acceptance (each followed by the counters): MCP `kb_create`/`kb_update`/`kb_delete`; CLI `create`/`delete`; a hand-added file followed by `index sync`; a KB never synced since `init`; an empty KB; a KB with a non-entry `README.md`.

### 4. Options

- **A (recommended).** Derive the count in `get_kb`, `health_kb` and `get_kb_stats`, using `list_kbs`'s subquery, and make `entry_count` equal `actual_count` there. Set `healthy = path_exists and not health_verdict(IndexManager(...).check_health(name))["is_unhealthy"]`, keeping `file_count` as information. Keep the column (dropping it is a schema migration for no gain) but stop reading it.
- **B.** Update the column on every `KBService` write. This writes derived state and enforces the rule call site by call site; principles 4 and 8 rule it out.
- **C.** Derive the count only and keep the 10% rule. This is smaller, but `healthy` still disagrees with `index health` on a KB that has a README.

### 5. Open questions

- `check_health` walks the KB. `health_kb` already does `rglob`, so the cost is similar. Measure it on this repo's `kb/` before choosing.
- Should `get_kb_stats` keep both keys (a public field on REST `StatsResponse`) with equal values, or drop `actual_count`? Keeping both with equal values breaks no client.

```
Acceptance:   for each shape above, kb_registry_health / kb health / GET /api/kbs/{name}/health report
              entry_count == the index's count and healthy == (index health is not unhealthy); kb_stats
              and /api/stats report entry_count == actual_count. Fails today: two kb_create, then
              kb_registry_health → entry_count 0, healthy false.
Regimes:      KB never synced; KB folder missing (path_exists false → healthy false, unchanged); KB with
              non-entry .md files
Touches:      existing: pyrite/services/kb_registry_service.py (get_kb, health_kb), pyrite/storage/kb_ops.py
              (get_kb_stats), pyrite/services/kb_service.py (list_kbs fallback)   new: tests/test_kb_counts_are_derived.py, changelog.d/<n>.fixed.md
Sequence:     independent
Model:        sonnet
heavy:        no
Cold read:    no
Out of scope: dropping the KB.entry_count column (a migration; nothing needs it gone)
```

**Checked versus assumed.** Ran: MCP `kb_create` ×2, `kb_registry_health`, `kb_stats`; CLI `kb health`, `kb list`, `index health`. Assumed: the REST health route returns the same dict (it calls `health_kb`). **This groom is wrong if** a caller relies on `entry_count` meaning "count at last sync" (none found by grep). Footprint: 3 source files and 1 test, about 120 lines.

items.title: Restore the mcp_adapter_pre_tool_call and mcp_adapter_tool_call_result filters

labels.name: safety
labels.description: Part of making Shim the safest WordPress MCP plugin

items.body:
## Problem

Since 0.5.0, upstream MCP Adapter lets code inspect, change or block tool-call arguments before execution and transform results after it. Shim's fork predates that, so there is no supported way to add logging, redaction, approval or policy checks around a tool call without patching the plugin. The audit log (#57) and confirmations (#56) both need this seam.

## Evidence

- Upstream 0.6.2 `includes/Handlers/Tools/ToolsHandler.php` applies `mcp_adapter_pre_tool_call` (and short-circuits on a `WP_Error`) and `mcp_adapter_tool_call_result`.
- Shim's [`ToolsHandler.php`](https://github.com/justadityaraj/shim-mcp/blob/v1.1.0/includes/Server/Handlers/Tools/ToolsHandler.php#L334) has no `apply_filters()` call. The ability runs with the raw arguments at L334.

## Minimal fix

Port both filters with upstream's names, arguments and order:

- `$args = apply_filters( 'mcp_adapter_pre_tool_call', $args, $tool_name, $tool, $server )` before execution; a `WP_Error` return stops the call and becomes an MCP error result.
- `$result = apply_filters( 'mcp_adapter_tool_call_result', $result, $args, $tool_name, $tool, $server )` after execution, before the response is built.

## Done when

- Both filters fire once for every `tools/call` over stdio and HTTP.
- A `WP_Error` from the pre filter stops the call and returns an error result, and the ability does not run.
- A `tests/wp/` test hooks both filters and checks the arguments and the short-circuit.
- The README lists both filters.

`repolens mcp` (#10) works with any MCP client that starts a stdio server, but the docs only
show how to add it to Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. Add the setup for other clients people
use, for example:

- VS Code (GitHub Copilot)
- Windsurf
- Zed
- Gemini CLI
- Cline
- Continue
- JetBrains AI Assistant

**Where to start** the "`repolens mcp`" section of [docs/cli.md](https://github.com/Douglas-Strey/repolens-cli/blob/main/docs/cli.md#repolens-mcp),
which has a block per client, and its Portuguese mirror in `docs/pt-BR/cli.md` (code blocks
stay identical; `test/docs/links.test.ts` checks it). The README section stays short: add a
client there only if it is widely used.

For each client:

- **Link its official documentation in the PR**, and use the config format it documents
  (file location, JSON or TOML shape, the command and arguments).
- **Say where the server starts.** If the client doesn't start servers in the project
  directory, pass the project as an argument, using the client's variable for it when it has
  one (Cursor uses `${workspaceFolder}`).
- **Mention any startup timeout.** If it is short, say so: the first `npx` run downloads
  RepoLens (see the Codex note).
- **Test it if you can**, and say in the PR which client version you tried.

---

**Want to take it?** Comment here first so two people don't build the same thing, then read
[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Douglas-Strey/repolens-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
One PR can cover several clients.

items.title: Examples: use the MCP server from Python agent frameworks
items.body:
**Why:** people building their own agents can give them pubchem-finder's 17 tools through MCP, without touching the Python API. A small `examples/` folder would show how, one short runnable script per framework. Part of #23.

**Proposal:** add `examples/` with scripts like these. One framework per PR is fine.
- **Plain MCP Python client:** `stdio_client` + `ClientSession`, list the tools, call `compound_properties` and `similarity_search`. [`scripts/smoke.py`](https://github.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/blob/master/scripts/smoke.py) and [`tests/e2e/test_stdio.py`](https://github.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/blob/master/tests/e2e/test_stdio.py) already do this and are a good starting point. It needs no API key, so CI could run it.
- **OpenAI Agents SDK** with `MCPServerStdio` ([docs](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/mcp/)).
- **LangChain / LangGraph** with [`langchain-mcp-adapters`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-mcp-adapters) (`MultiServerMCPClient`, stdio).
- Others welcome: PydanticAI, LlamaIndex, the Claude Agent SDK...

**Conventions**
- Each script is short (well under 100 lines) and declares its own dependencies with [inline script metadata](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/scripts/#declaring-script-dependencies), so `uv run examples/<name>.py` just works and the framework stays out of pubchem-finder's dependencies.
- Start the server with `command="uvx", args=["pubchem-finder", "mcp"]`.
- Ask one realistic question, e.g. *"Find close analogues of aspirin in the local index and summarise what changed"* (needs `uvx pubchem-finder index build --limit 1`), or a PubChem lookup that needs no index.
- Read API keys from the environment, and say which one at the top of the file.
- Link the folder from the README's "Use it from Python" section.

**Done when** at least one framework example runs as described, with the exact command and its output in the PR.
